summary: Backend testing for Delivery Tracker. Imported the real-world Brazilian SLA CSV (1731 rows, semicolon, UTF-8 BOM, DD/MM/YY) via /api/import/csv and validated all downstream endpoints. 25/25 pytest tests pass on the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. CSV import returns the expected totals (total_rows=1731, late=57, on_time=1534, pending=134, excluded=6). Late detection logic, dashboard aggregations, orders filters/search/pagination, late report CSV (with BOM + semicolon + Content-Disposition), and tickets CRUD (incl. 409 duplicate, 400 invalid status, 404 unknown id) all behave as specified. _id (ObjectId) is never leaked in any response.

minor.issue: Sort key is only days_late (many ties at 0). Without a stable secondary sort key, paginated requests can return overlapping documents across pages. Add a tie-breaker like .sort([('days_late', -1), ('id', 1)]).

Import is not atomic: db.orders.delete_many({}) runs before insert_many. If insert_many fails midway, all previous data is lost. Consider buffering, then doing delete+insert in a transaction or insert-first-with-import_id then delete-others.
Heuristic for sniffing encoding/sep relies on raising StopIteration to break loops; fragile. Works today, but worth refactoring to explicit sniffing (csv.Sniffer or pre-scan for ';' vs ',').
No auth/rate limiting on a destructive DELETE /api/import which wipes the whole orders + tickets collections.

action_items: (Optional) Add stable secondary sort key for /api/orders to make pagination deterministic.
(Optional) Make /api/import/csv atomic (don't delete existing data until new docs are validated/inserted).
(Optional) Consider auth on DELETE /api/import to avoid accidental data wipe.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~550 lines and still maintainable, but should be split soon (helpers/parse, models, routers/import, routers/orders, routers/tickets) before adding more features.

_compute_late() correctly handles excluded statuses (cancelada/devolvida/extraviada) and treats 'entregue' OR data_entrega presence as delivered. Edge case: if a row has data_entrega filled but situacao is empty, code treats it as delivered (correct behavior for this dataset).
Date parsing tries multiple formats and pandas fallback — robust.
All find()/aggregate() projections explicitly exclude _id (good). create_ticket() also pops _id before returning (good).
CSV download adds BOM and semicolon — Excel-friendly (good).
seed_data_creation: Imported the real CSV from https://customer-assets.emergentagent.com/job_sheet-error-resolve/artifacts/zgamyd3p_relatorio_sla_26_04_2026.csv (saved to /tmp/relatorio_sla.csv). Final test (test_zz_clear_data) wipes the dataset, so the DB is empty after the run; main agent should re-import via the UI/API to repopulate before manual verification.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green on iteration 1. Real CSV is at /tmp/relatorio_sla.csv. Tests at /app/backend/tests/test_delivery_tracker.py auto-import it on session start and clear data at the end. Expected counts: total=1731, late=57, on_time=1534, pending=134, excluded=6. Frontend UI testing was explicitly out-of-scope for this iteration.
